points.reason: The request address is copied and split into tag and index values, then reconstructed onto the backing-bus address, so it can be observed or redirected here.
The clocked tag and index state can be changed and thereby alter the reconstructed access address.
The address input is decoded into tag, index and word-offset indices that select cache state and data locations.
The read/write field selects acknowledgement, cache write enable, refill, or direct backing-bus behavior.
The registered controller state preserves the path selected from the read/write direction.
The request byte-enable field is used as the cache write-enable value.
The write-enable bits select which byte arrays receive the write data.
Address-region, atomic, and debug conditions set the bypass decision, which selects direct backing-bus handling instead of the normal cache path.
The registered bypass decision controls whether the next lookup uses the direct path.
The memory instance receives consequences of the bypass decision but the RTL shows no separate bypass decision stored or observed inside that block.
The valid and tag comparison produces hit_o; the resulting hit or miss changes acknowledgement and refill timing.
The hit signal selects immediate acknowledgement or a refill, making residency observable through response timing and changing the selected behavior.
The registered state preserves the hit-dependent path and can cause the controller to take an incorrect or stalled path.
The controller generates refill addresses, write commands, and completion transitions, and waits for backing-bus acknowledgements.
The registered refill state and word offset preserve progress and determine whether the next refill request is issued.
The memory instance receives the refill address, data, write enables, and new-line command that determine whether the line is filled correctly.
A pending fence selects the clear state, commands cache invalidation, and optionally emits the external fence request.
The registered pending-fence flag can repeatedly divert the controller into the clear operation.
The clear command clears all cache-valid bits and can therefore remove cached state or repeatedly prevent normal hits.
The bus error is accumulated, then controls invalidation, the host error response, and abort of the refill.
The registered accumulated error persists across refill words and controls recovery.
The accumulated error causes the selected cache line to be invalidated after a failed refill.
The refill-error state decides whether cache invalidation is issued and whether the operation returns an error.
The registered error state controls the later invalidation recovery decision.
The invalidation command clears the selected line's valid bit, preventing failed refill data from remaining valid.
